fact_en:
Why does gliding save energy?

Gliding uses less energy than true flying because the animal doesn't need to flap its wings.
fact_bis:
Nganong mas makatipig og kusog ang pagdagan-dagan?

Mas makatipig og kusog ang pagdagan-dagan kaysa tinuod nga paglupad kay dili na kinahanglan ikampayng mga pako.

findings.note: Whole card is about gliding, and both the question and the answer call it 'pagdagan-dagan' (running/scampering around) with no air context in the question: 'Nganong mas makatipig og kusog ang pagdagan-dagan?' A child reads that running around saves energy compared to real flying because you don't have to flap wings — the concept of gliding (staying airborne without flapping) is never named. Cebuano for glide is 'modahili' / 'molutaw', which this same corpus uses correctly in the colugo card ffct-06090 ('modahili gikan sa kahoy paingon sa kahoy').

fact_en:
Which mammal is the only one that can truly fly?

The bat! Unlike the colugo, which only glides, bats are the only mammals capable of true flight.
fact_bis:
Unsang mammal lang ang tinuod nga makalupad?

Ang kabog! Dili sama sa colugo nga nagdagan-dagan lang, ang kabog lamang ang mammal nga makalupad gyud.

findings.note: 'Dili sama sa colugo nga nagdagan-dagan lang' for 'Unlike the colugo, which only glides' — states flatly that the colugo just runs around, with no 'sa hangin' to rescue it, and the card never corrects it. The headline fact (the bat is the only truly flying mammal) does survive, so this is the weaker of the two, but the contrast the card is built on is reversed into a false claim about the colugo.

fact_en: Sometimes a deep wound leaves a scar even after it has completely healed.
fact_bis: Usahay, ang lawom nga samad mubilin og piklat bisan naayo na kini.

findings.note: title_bis 'Lawom nga Samad Peke' = 'deep wound fake'. 'Peke' means counterfeit in this corpus (platypus ffct-01802, fool's gold ffct-32719, kwek-kwek ffct-17499); the intended word is 'peklat'/'piklat' (scar), which the body does use. Title-field defect: the card face states a different thing, though the body restores the fact.

fact_en:
Why can a pufferfish balloon up?

A pufferfish has no ribs around its belly like other animals — so nothing stops it from puffing up big when it fills with water!
fact_bis:
Nganong modako ang butete?

Ang butete walay gusok sa tiyan sama sa ubang mananap — mao nga walay makababag aron modako ang lawas niini kon mapuno og tubig!

findings.note: title_bis 'Butete Walay Gukod' = 'pufferfish has no chase/pursuit'; the fact is ribs ('gusok', used correctly in the body). Same title typo recurs in ffct-00431 ('Gukod nga Bantay sa Baga' on a rib-cage card), so the pair is worth greping — 'gukod' legitimately means chase in ffct-28499 / dcard-03520, never ribs. Body does restore 'gusok', so this is a title-field defect, not a lost fact.

fact_en:
How does water rise up inside a tall tree?

As water evaporates from tiny leaf pores, it pulls more water up through the xylem from the roots — just like sucking water through a straw!
fact_bis:
Giunsa pagsaka sa tubig sa sulod sa kahoy?

Samtang nagsuyop ang tubig sa stomata, naghila kini og tubig pataas sa xylem gikan sa gamot — sama sa paghigop sa tubig gamit ang straw!

findings.note: Transpiration direction reversed at the leaf. EN: 'As water evaporates from tiny leaf pores, it pulls more water up through the xylem.' BIS: 'Samtang nagsuyop ang tubig sa stomata, naghila kini og tubig pataas sa xylem' — 'suyop' is suck/absorb (used that way elsewhere in the corpus: lorikeet tongue, remora sucker), so the Cebuano says water is being sucked IN at the stomata, the opposite of evaporating out. Evaporation is never mentioned; sibling cards render this correctly with 'alisngaw'/'mogawas' (ffct-01646, ffct-04162). A child reads that water enters through the leaf pores.

fact_en: Ginger and galangal don't stay in one spot — they spread through rhizomes, underground stems that sprout new shoots from their nodes so the plant keeps multiplying!
fact_bis: Ang luya ug lagkaw dili lang magpabilin sa usa ka lugar — mikatag sila pinaagi sa rhizome, usa ka tangkay ilawom sa yuta nga nagpatubo og bag-ong turok gikan sa mga node niini!

findings.note: EN names ginger and galangal; BIS says 'Ang luya ug lagkaw'. 'Lagkaw' is a hut/shed, not a plant — galangal is 'langkawas' (zero corpus hits; 'lagkaw' appears only in this card). Never corrected anywhere on the card, so the second example plant is a different thing entirely.

fact_en: During floods in the Philippines, drinking water can mix with human waste. Germs in dirty water can cause cholera and typhoid — that's why boiling or filtering water keeps it safe to drink.
fact_bis: Panahon sa baha sa Pilipinas, usahay masagol ang hugaw sa imnonon nga tubig. Ang germs sa hugaw nga tubig makahatag og cholera ug typhoid — mao nga luwas ra imnon ang tubig kon pakuanon o paagion sa filter.

findings.note: The safety instruction is lost. EN: 'boiling or filtering water keeps it safe to drink.' BIS: 'luwas ra imnon ang tubig kon pakuanon o paagion sa filter'. 'Pakuanon' is not a word for boiling — it reads as 'have it whatchamacallit-ed' from the filler 'kuan' (the only other corpus hit, ffct-24137, is the same filler artifact). Cebuano for boil is 'pakuluon' / 'pabukalon' (the corpus uses 'pagkulo', 'pagpabukal' elsewhere). Child gets only 'filter it', and this is a flood/cholera card.

fact_en:
How does camouflage protect animals?

Many animals have colors or patterns that match their surroundings — this is called camouflage. It makes them hard for predators to spot, keeping them safer!
fact_bis:
Giunsa pagtabang sa camouflage sa mananap?

Daghang mananap ang adunay kolor o pattern nga susama sa ilang palibot — gitawag kini og camouflage. Tungod niini, lisod sila makita sa mga mananap nga mokaon nila, busa mas luwas sila!

findings.note: title_bis "Camouflage Mangayam" says camouflage HUNTS (mangayam = to hunt), reversing the card's point — English title is "Camouflage Hides Animals" and the body is about prey being hard for predators to spot. No other camouflage card in the corpus uses a hunting word (they use Camouflage / Pagtago / Kamuplong / Pagtakoban); cf. the same misuse in ffct-10579.

fact_en: Some millipedes release a bad-smelling chemical to drive away animals that try to eat them.
fact_bis: Ang ubang millipede mogawas og baho nga kemikal aron abugon ang mga hayop nga buot mokaon kanila.

findings.note: title_bis "Alupihan" names a centipede, not the millipede the card is about. The corpus itself keeps the two apart (Centipede => "Alupihan" in ffct-00140/00581/01719; Millipede => "Milipid" in ffct-00135/01041/03115, and ffct-03345 "Alupihan ug Milipid" uses both side by side), so the Cebuano title names a different animal. The body only ever says the English "millipede", so nothing in the Cebuano corrects it.

fact_en:
Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?

No — that popping sound is just gas bubbles bursting in the fluid that lubricates your joints.
fact_bis:
Makahatag ba og arthritis ang pag-crack sa bukog?

Dili — ang tingog gikan ra sa pagputok sa mga gas bubble sa likido nga naghapohap sa imong mga lutahan.

findings.note: title_bis "Crack Kuko Gas" puts the cracking in the fingernails (kuko = nail/claw) instead of the knuckles/finger joints of the English "Knuckle Gas Bubbles". The body says "pag-crack sa bukog" and mentions "lutahan", so the joint is never named in the title's terms — a child reading the title alone gets the wrong body part.

fact_en: The slow-moving dugong has a thick layer of fat under its skin that keeps it warm and helps it float easily.
fact_bis: Ang hinay nga dugong adunay baga nga tambok ilawom sa panit nga makatabang aron magpabilin nga init ug sayon molutaw.

findings.note: title_bis "Tambok Dugong Lupad" says the dugong's fat FLIES (lupad) where the English title is "Dugong Fat Floats"; float is lutaw, which the body correctly uses ("sayon molutaw"). Read on its own the title states something physically false about a sea mammal.

fact_en:
What is the Palawan pangolin?

The Palawan pangolin is an endangered scaly animal that eats ants and termites — sadly, it's one of the world's most trafficked animals.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang Palawan pangolin?

Ang Palawan pangolin usa ka nagmeligro nga mananap nga adunay talagsaon nga kaliskis ug mokaon og langgam ug anay — sa makasubo, usa kini sa labing gipamaligya nga mananap sa kalibutan.

findings.note: EN 'eats ants and termites' -> BIS 'mokaon og langgam ug anay'. In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (same batch, ffct-06517: 'Ang manok langgam' = a chicken is a bird); the Tagalog sense langgam = ant does not apply. anay (termite) is right, so the Cebuano card says the pangolin eats birds and termites. Ants appear nowhere on the card, so the fact is unrecoverable from the Cebuano alone.
